key_insight: Non-Gaussian bosonic inputs can beat the best Gaussian thermal-state bound and certify positive quantum capacity in noise regimes where all single-mode Gaussian states fail.
engineering_relevance: This widens the usable operating window for bosonic quantum links, showing that carefully engineered non-Gaussian encoding can preserve quantum communication at higher thermal noise.
method: Proved the Holevo–Werner thermal-state lower bound is optimal within all single-mode Gaussian inputs.
Constructed an explicit rank-two non-Gaussian state supported on six Fock levels.
Compared analytic witnesses with numerical optimization over non-Gaussian families.
evidence_signal: At ν=1, they certify positive coherent information down to η=0.7841; at η=0.8 with one thermal photon, Gaussian inputs give non-positive coherent information, while a rank-two witness reaches at least 4.7×10^-4 qubits/use and numerical non-Gaussian optimization reaches 8.4×10^-3 qubits/use.
watch_item: The demonstrated advantage relies on specialized non-Gaussian states and the certified rates are small, so practical implementation will depend on state preparation precision and robust decoding.
paper_title: Bosonic quantum communication beyond the thermal threshold
